# Settings reference

Status: generated
Owner: src/config/

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-settings-reference.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every setting in `~/.atomic-agent/config.json` (config version 79), with its type, default and description, followed by the settings that only exist as environment variables. Defaults are what a fresh install gets; migrations and env variables can make an existing install differ.

Read or change a setting from the terminal:

```sh
atomic-agent config list --describe      # this list, with your current values
atomic-agent config get agent.maxSteps
atomic-agent config set agent.maxSteps 40
atomic-agent config unset agent.maxSteps # back to the default
```

In the TUI, `/settings <words>` searches the same list. The desktop app shows it under Settings, Advanced, All settings. List-valued keys have no single-value form; set them with the whole-file JSON form (`atomic-agent config set -`).

## version

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `number` | `79` | The on-disk schema version. Usually `USER_CONFIG_VERSION`, but a file written by a NEWER build keeps its own (higher) number all the way through parse and write-back, so an older build can never label a newer file with its own version. See `parseUserConfigFile`. |

| `localModels.url` | `string` | `"http://127.0.0.1:9931"` |  |
| `localModels.mode` | `'external' \| 'managed'` | `"external"` | `external` uses `url`; `managed` overrides runtime `url` to localhost + `managed.port`. |
| `localModels.completionMaxTokens` | `number` | `16384` | Upper bound on `n_predict` for grammar-constrained tool-call completions. Range [64, 131072]. The env var, when set, still wins over this file value (operator override). Env `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_MAX_TOKENS` wins when set. |
| `localModels.requestTimeoutMs` | `number` | `300000` | Budget of one request to the local model: the whole request for a unary completion, the idle gap between bytes for a stream (see `RuntimeLocalModelsConfig.requestTimeoutMs`). Default 300 000 ms. `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, when set, still wins over this file value (ATO-922). Env `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` wins when set. |
| `localModels.useServerTemplate` | `'auto' \| 'on' \| 'off'` | `"auto"` | Render local prompts through the model's own chat template (llama-server `POST /apply-template`) instead of atag's hand-built framing. `auto` (default) uses the template for every family without a hand-built profile — everything but Gemma and Qwen — so Llama, GLM, Mistral and other GGUFs get their turn markers. |
| `localModels.thinking` | `'auto' \| 'on' \| 'off'` | `"auto"` | The template's thinking switch (`chat_template_kwargs: {enable_thinking}`) on server-templated prompts, for families whose template reads it. `auto` (default) leaves the template's own default; `on` / `off` set it. |
| `localModels.reasoningBudgetTokens` | `number` | `0` | How many tokens a local reasoning model may spend thinking before a tool call, on the grammar path. The GBNF prelude bounds the think block at `reasoningBudgetTokens × 4` characters; past that the sampler admits only the close sentinel, so the model is forced to close the block and emit the call. `0` leaves the prelude unbounded. |
| `localModels.drySampler` | `boolean` | `false` | Turn on llama.cpp's DRY ("don't repeat yourself") sampler for every `/completion` request to a llama.cpp-family engine (Atomic Core, the managed llama-server, an External llama-server). It penalises a token that would extend a sequence already in the last 256 tokens of prompt plus reply, which targets the verbatim prose loops small models fall into. |
| `localModels.managed.engine` | `'llama-server' \| 'atomic-core'` | `"atomic-core"` | Managed process owner. Default `"atomic-core"`; files before v77 migrate to it (llama.cpp stays selectable). |
| `localModels.managed.modelId` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `localModels.managed.port` | `number` | `19091` |  |
| `localModels.managed.dataDirOverride` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `localModels.managed.autoUpdate` | `boolean` | `true` | When true, managed-mode start (TUI auto-start / `s`, CLI `models start`) checks GitHub Releases and replaces the llama.cpp zip if a newer tag (or a stale Windows variant) is available. Default `true` since config v41. Older files stored an unused `false` default — those migrate to `true`. Set `false` to pin the installed backend. |
| `localModels.managed.stopOnExit` | `boolean` | `true` | Stop the managed chat daemon when the last CLI session exits. `true` (default) — closing the terminal frees the RAM/VRAM the model was holding; a second live session keeps the daemon up (see `session-registry.ts`). `false` — keep the model warm between sessions; the operator stops it via `atomic-agent models stop`. |
| `localModels.managed.autoRestart` | `boolean` | `true` | Bring the managed chat daemon back by itself when it dies (or, from the wedge watchdog, stops answering) while this TUI owns it. `true` (default): a crashed or killed llama-server is restarted within a few seconds and a parked turn resumes on it; three deaths within a minute of their start stop the retries and name the fault. |
| `localModels.managed.device` | `string` | `"auto"` | Compute-device preference for the managed llama.cpp daemon: - `"auto"` (default) — enumerate via `llama-server --list-devices` at start and pick the best discrete GPU; CPU fallback when none. - a concrete backend device id (e.g. `"Vulkan0"`) — pin offload to that device. - `"cpu"` — force CPU-only (`-ngl 0`). |
| `localModels.managed.backendVariant` | `'auto' \| 'cpu' \| 'vulkan' \| 'cuda-12.4' \| 'cuda-13.3'` | `"auto"` | Which llama.cpp build (release zip) the managed backend installs. Windows-only — every other platform, Linux arm64 included, publishes a single asset, so there is nothing for the preference to choose between and it is ignored there. |
| `localModels.managed.coreBackendVariant` | `'auto' \| 'cpu'` | `"auto"` | Which build Atomic Core installs on Windows x64 (the `atomic-core` engine; `backendVariant` above is the llama-server engine's). - `"auto"` (default) — Core's recommendation for this hardware. - `"cpu"` — Core's CPU build. |
| `localModels.managed.contextSize` | `number` | `0` | llama-server context window (`--ctx-size`) for the managed chat daemon. |
| `localModels.managed.tensorSplit` | `number[]` | `[]` | Multi-GPU tensor split for the managed chat daemon. Empty (the default) keeps the single-device behavior: `device` auto-picks the best GPU and pins offload there. Two or more non-negative ratios (at least one positive, e.g. |
| `localModels.managed.parallel` | `number \| 'auto'` | `"auto"` | llama-server request slots (`--parallel`) for the managed chat daemon: `"auto"` (the default since config v63) or a pinned 1..8. |
| `localModels.managed.swaFull` | `'auto' \| 'on' \| 'off'` | `"auto"` | `--swa-full` for a sliding-window model (Gemma 4 and kin): keep the whole context in the sliding layers so a partially matching prompt reuses its matching prefix instead of re-reading everything — at a several-fold KV cost for those layers. - `"auto"` (default) — on when the full-SWA KV estimate fits the launch's memory budget (see `swa-full.ts`), else off. |

Catalogue and custom-model URLs stay canonical `https://huggingface.co/...`; the endpoint is applied at request time, so switching it never invalidates a partial download. The `HF_ENDPOINT` env var (what `huggingface_hub` honours) wins over this value when set. |

## agent

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent.tokenBudget` | `number` | `3000` | Compact target for the upper prompt. Its only remaining effect on a built prompt is the `### session-facts` + `### loaded-skills` share, and `sessionSectionsMaxTokens` now overrides that directly; the stable prefix is sized by what it contains, not by this number. |
| `agent.maxSteps` | `number` | `25` | Steps in one leg of a task — a checkpoint, not the end of it. |
| `agent.providerWait.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` restores the old behaviour: fail the turn immediately. |
| `agent.providerWait.maxWaitMs` | `number` | `300000` | Give up (and fail the turn) after waiting this long in one outage. |
| `agent.task.maxSteps` | `number` | `1000` | Hard ceiling on steps for one task. Reached, the loop spends its last step summarising instead of being cut off mid-edit. |
| `agent.task.maxDurationMs` | `number` | `7200000` | Wall-clock ceiling for one task. Same graceful ending. |
| `agent.task.autoContinue` | `boolean` | `true` | Carry on past a leg boundary while the work is progressing. Off means the historical behaviour: stop at `agent.maxSteps`. |
| `agent.task.resumeInterrupted` | `boolean` | `true` | Continue a durable task whose run a crash, a kill or a restart cut off, from its session's per-step checkpoint, with a note telling the model how far it got (ATO-1109). Off: the run starts over from the task's message, as before. A run a person stopped is never resumed. |
| `agent.task.maxResumes` | `number` | `3` | Resumes after the agent died under a task (crash or kill) before the task is failed instead: the guard against a task that takes the agent down every time. `0` fails it at the first such interruption. |
| `agent.task.maxCostUsd` | `number` | `0` | Spend ceiling for one task, in USD, estimated from each completion's usage and the model's prices (prompt-cache aware). Reached, the task ends the same graceful way as the time ceiling. `0` means no cap. Unpriced models (a local model) count as $0, so this never stops local work. Default `0`. |
| `agent.toolTimeoutMs` | `number` | `60000` |  |
| `agent.readScope` | `'working-dir' \| 'unrestricted'` | `"working-dir"` | Where a session's reads may go. `working-dir` (the default) confines filesystem reads and shell path arguments to the working directory and the paths the user named in the conversation; `unrestricted` is the pre-v67 behaviour. |
| `agent.approvalLevel` | `1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5` | `1` | Five-step approval ladder. Replaces the binary `approvalRequired`; the legacy key is still read once for migration (see `resolveApprovalLevel`) and never written back. |
| `agent.compaction.auto` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `agent.compaction.mode` | `'auto' \| 'model' \| 'extractive'` | `"auto"` |  |
| `agent.compaction.triggerRatio` | `number` | `0.9` |  |
| `agent.compaction.targetRatio` | `number` | `0.65` |  |
| `agent.compaction.summaryMaxTokens` | `number` | `2048` |  |
| `agent.compaction.reasoningReserveTokens` | `number` | `4096` | Output tokens a summary call may spend on reasoning on top of `summaryMaxTokens`. A thinking model writes its reasoning out of the same reply allowance; without room for it the summary is cut off. The summary itself is still held to `summaryMaxTokens`. Small windows get less (see `compactionReplyBudget`); `0` sends no reserve. |
| `agent.compaction.timeoutMs` | `number` | `600000` | Timeout of one summary call; the total budget scales with chunk count. |
| `agent.compaction.maxTotalTimeoutMs` | `number` | `600000` |  |
| `agent.compaction.background` | `boolean` | `true` | Under `auto`, extend a rolling summary between turns so compaction can swap it in without a model call. Optional: absent means on. It still runs only where it is safe and worthwhile (see the runtime's background scheduler); `false` turns it off everywhere. |
| `agent.conversationMaxTokens` | `number` | `0` |  |
| `agent.conversationMaxPairs` | `number` | `200` | How many macro-turns of history the prompt carries — one "pair" being a task you sent plus everything the agent did answering it. |
| `agent.nameSessions` | `boolean` | `true` | Ask the model to name each session. |
| `agent.conversationLowWater` | `number` | `0.65` | Share of a limit the transcript keeps after a cut, `(0, 1]`. History is dropped in chunks — down to this share of the token budget or of `conversationMaxPairs`, whichever overflowed — and the cut then holds until the next overflow, so the prompt is append-only in between and a local model reuses its KV cache. |
| `agent.sessionSectionsMaxTokens` | `number` | `0` | Ceiling on `### session-facts` + `### loaded-skills` combined. One cap over two sections because one `truncateToTokens` call trims the two as a single blob, facts first, so the skill bodies at its tail are what a cut takes. |
| `agent.worldSnapshotMaxTokens` | `number` | `8000` | Safety-net ceiling for the `### world` section. ARIA snapshots are already compressed at the browser layer; this cap guards against edge cases where compression misses (huge SVG trees, etc.). |
| `agent.smartApproval` | `boolean` | `false` | Smart approval (ATO-465). When on, a request that would prompt, of a category the operator could grant for the session, is first rated by a model (`src/approval/risk-review.ts`): `low` runs it without a prompt, anything else and every failure prompts as before, with the rating shown. Off by default. Read live: no restart needed. |
| `agent.smartApprovalModel` | `string \| null` | `null` | The `llm.providers[].id` the risk review runs on. `null` (default): a local `llama-server` link that has a model, else the active provider. |
| `agent.prompt.compact` | `'auto' \| 'on' \| 'off'` | `"auto"` | Stable-prefix shape. `compact` (default `"auto"`): the short scaffold for small context windows; `auto` turns it on when the model's known window is at most 64K tokens. See `src/prompt/compact-prompt.ts`. |
| `agent.tools.search` | `'auto' \| 'on' \| 'off'` | `"auto"` | Tool catalog on demand (ATO-558): `tools.search` is `auto`, `on` or `off`. Optional so configs and fixtures written before it stay valid; the parser always fills it. |

## web

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `web.search.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `web.search.provider` | `'duckduckgo' \| 'searxng' \| 'exa' \| 'brave'` | `"exa"` | Primary provider. The default `exa` uses its API endpoint when its `apiKeyEnv` resolves to a key, and its free keyless tier otherwise, with `duckduckgo` appended to the chain when it lacks it. The free tier runs out fast; a 429 parks it and the search result asks for a key (ATO-327). Existing configs need no rewrite for that. |
| `web.search.maxResults` | `number` | `8` |  |
| `web.search.timeoutMs` | `number` | `15000` |  |
| `web.search.cacheTtlMinutes` | `number` | `60` | Per-runtime result cache TTL in minutes. `0` disables caching. The cache is the primary defence against provider rate-limiting on repeated queries. |
| `web.search.persistCache` | `boolean` | `true` | Persist the result cache and the provider cooldown under `stateDir` (v46, #256), so a campaign that runs one process per task inherits both instead of starting cold and re-spending quota on queries the last process already answered. Key/TTL/eviction semantics are unchanged — only the storage moves. |
| `web.search.fallback` | `WebSearchProviderName[]` | `["duckduckgo"]` | Ordered fallback providers tried (after the primary) when a search is blocked / empty / throws. Default `["duckduckgo"]` — DuckDuckGo's keyless HTML endpoint, which also takes over from a keyless Exa primary that hit its free limit. |
| `web.search.searxng.instanceUrl` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `web.search.exa.endpoint` | `string` | `"https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp"` |  |
| `web.search.exa.apiEndpoint` | `string` | `"https://api.exa.ai/search"` |  |
| `web.search.exa.apiKeyEnv` | `string` | `"EXA_API_KEY"` |  |
| `web.search.brave.apiKeyEnv` | `string` | `"BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY"` |  |
| `web.fetch.timeoutMs` | `number` | `30000` | Overall per-attempt budget in milliseconds, passed to curl `--max-time`. Kept at the historical 30_000 so unconfigured installs behave exactly as before. A per-call `timeoutMs` tool argument overrides it. |
| `web.fetch.connectTimeoutMs` | `number` | `10000` | TCP/TLS connect budget in milliseconds, passed to curl `--connect-timeout`. Much smaller than `timeoutMs` because a host that has not completed a handshake in 10s is almost never merely slow — it is firewalled, dead, or blackholing packets, and waiting the full overall budget for it is pure loss. |
| `web.fetch.maxRetries` | `number` | `2` | Extra attempts after the first for retryable failures (429/502/503/504 and curl exit 28 "operation timed out"). `0` disables retrying. Deliberately small: `os.web.fetch` is GET-only, so retries are always safe, but each one spends task budget. |
| `web.fetch.retryBaseDelayMs` | `number` | `500` | Base delay in milliseconds for exponential backoff between retries (attempt N waits `retryBaseDelayMs * 2^(N-1)`). A server-sent `Retry-After` header wins over the computed delay when it is shorter than the cap. |
| `web.fetch.retryMaxDelayMs` | `number` | `5000` | Upper bound in milliseconds on any single backoff wait, including one derived from `Retry-After`. Stops a hostile or overloaded origin from parking the agent for minutes on a header value. |

| `projects.roots` | `string[]` | `[]` | Project path resolution. `roots` lists directories whose direct children are the user's projects; `os.fs.locate_project` matches fuzzy project names against them (one level, never recursive). ## tools

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tools.shell.defaultTimeoutMs` | `number` | `600000` | Wall-clock wait, in milliseconds, for an `os.shell.run` call whose `timeoutMs` the model omitted. Default 600 000 (10 min). A command still running then is not killed: it is detached as a job the model can `wait` for or `kill`, with its output so far in the result. `0` = no default, which is the pre-v67 behaviour. |
| `tools.shell.jobMaxMs` | `number` | `3600000` | Absolute ceiling, in milliseconds, for a detached job, counted from its start — kept or not, waited on or not. Default 3 600 000 (1 h). A positive integer. |
| `tools.shell.maxJobs` | `number` | `3` | Detached jobs that may run at once per session. Default 3. The next detach stops the oldest un-kept job first and says so. A positive integer. |
| `tools.shell.envPassthrough` | `string[]` | `["GITHUB_TOKEN","NOTION_API_KEY"]` | Variables an `os.shell.run` command inherits from the agent's environment even though they look like secrets. Without this, a command gets the agent's environment minus anything named like a KEY, TOKEN, SECRET or PASSWORD and the known provider keys (see `src/sandbox/command-env.ts`). |
| `tools.screen.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Computer use on macOS (ATO-525): `os.screen.capture` takes screenshots (asking as `screen_capture` below approval level 3) and `os.screen.{click,type,key}` drive the real mouse and keyboard, each input asking as `screen_control` below level 4. Default `false`: opt-in, and read at start, so turning it on takes a restart. |
| `tools.screen.point` | `boolean` | `true` | "Show where to click" on macOS (ATO-1018): `os.screen.point` draws arrows, boxes and labels through the desktop app's overlay and never clicks or types, and `os.screen.capture` comes with it (still asking as `screen_capture`) so the model can see what it points at. Default `true`; independent of `enabled`. Read at start. |

## sessions

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions.retention.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Default `false`: the operator opts in. |
| `sessions.retention.maxAgeDays` | `number \| null` | `90` | Age cutoff in days against `updated_at`. Default 90. A positive integer, or `null` for no age rule (leaving `maxRows` as the only thing that prunes). Note that `undefined` takes the default and an explicit `null` does not — clearing the rule is a choice, not an omission. |
| `sessions.retention.maxRows` | `number \| null` | `null` | Hard cap on stored sessions; anything past it goes oldest first. Default `null` (no cap) — a row count means nothing without knowing how the operator works, so age is the rule that ships on. |

## tracing

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tracing.trace.enabled` | `boolean \| null` | `null` | Trace recording toggle. - `true` / `false`: explicit user choice (wins over the entry-point default). - `null`: defer to the entry point. `createAgentRuntime` resolves it via `traceDefault`: CLI / TUI / serve use `true`, sidecar uses `false`. This keeps local debugging observable by default while embedded hosts stay silent unless they opt in. |
| `tracing.trace.maxBytesPerSession` | `number` | `10485760` | Hard cap on a single session's trace file. Crossing it drops the OLDEST events, not the newest: the sink trims the head back to half the cap and keeps recording. |

Typed-NOTE extraction: when `enabled`, the reflection prompt forces every NOTE to carry a `[type=event\|behavior\|knowledge\|skill]` marker that the parser projects into a synthetic `type:X` tag on the stored memory. Default `false` — legacy untyped NOTEs are byte-stable. |

When `true`, the reflection prompt switches to `REFLECTION_STABLE_PREFIX_ANY_SPEAKER` so the extractor treats every named speaker in the USER channel — including third parties — as a valid source for SET / NOTE extraction. |

| `memory.index.maxTokens` | `number` | `300` | Safety-net ceiling for the rendered `### memory-index` section. |
| `memory.dedup.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `memory.dedup.fts5Threshold` | `number` | `0.85` |  |
| `memory.eviction.utilityWeighted` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `memory.eviction.maxAgeMs` | `number` | `2592000000` |  |
| `memory.embeddings.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `memory.embeddings.fts5Weight` | `number` | `0.5` |  |
| `memory.embeddings.vectorWeight` | `number` | `0.5` |  |
| `memory.embeddings.bruteForceCeiling` | `number` | `2000` |  |
| `memory.embeddings.backfill` | `boolean` | `true` | Embed, in the background, the notes that have no vector for the active embedding model (after a model switch, or when embeddings are turned on over an existing corpus). Default `true`. |
| `memory.links.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch (covers both recall expansion and link generation). |
| `memory.links.autoGenerate` | `boolean` | `true` | Fire the `link-generator` sub-call after main reflection. Set to `false` to keep the schema + expansion machinery but never grow the graph automatically (manual `LinkStore.add` still works). |
| `memory.links.expansionDepth` | `number` | `1` | BFS depth on recall. Clamped to [1, 3]. |
| `memory.links.maxExpanded` | `number` | `12` | Hard cap on expanded-id count per recall turn. |
| `memory.links.maxLinksPerCall` | `number` | `4` | Hard cap on persisted edges per link-generator call. |
| `memory.links.minCandidates` | `number` | `2` | Skip the LLM call when the surfaced set has fewer than this many ids (zero useful links possible). |
| `memory.links.generatorTimeoutMs` | `number` | `60000` | Hard timeout for the LLM call. |
| `memory.evolution.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch. Default `true`. |
| `memory.evolution.maxPerWrite` | `number` | `2` | Hard cap on number of EVOLVE directives actually applied per reflection. Default `2`. |
| `memory.evolution.leaseMs` | `number` | `60000` | B↔C lease window in ms. EVOLVE skips any target whose `consolidating_at` lies within `now - leaseMs`. Default `60000` (1 min). |
| `memory.lessons.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch for `### lessons` rendering + `memory.lessons.recall` + `ConsolidatorJob.start`. Default `true`. |
| `memory.lessons.recallK` | `number` | `2` | Top-K lessons surfaced per turn (BM25). Default `2`. |
| `memory.lessons.maxTokens` | `number` | `300` | Hard cap on the rendered `### lessons` block. Default `300`. |
| `memory.lessons.indexLimit` | `number` | `20` | Row cap on `LessonStore.listIndex`. Default `20`. |
| `memory.lessons.maxEntries` | `number` | `500` | Hard cap on active lessons. Default `500`. Phase 6 owns the deprecation sweep — phase 5 plumbs it dormant. |
| `memory.lessons.deprecationAgeMs` | `number` | `2592000000` | Phase 6 hook (still wired in phase 5): lessons with `success_count == 0` older than this become deprecated. Default `2_592_000_000` (30 days). |
| `memory.procedures.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch. Default `true`. |
| `memory.procedures.recallK` | `number` | `2` | Top-K procedures surfaced per turn via BM25 against the current user message. Default `2`. |
| `memory.procedures.maxTokens` | `number` | `400` | Hard cap on the rendered `### procedures` block. Default `400`. |
| `memory.procedures.indexLimit` | `number` | `20` | Row cap on `ProcedureStore.listIndex`. Default `20`. |
| `memory.procedures.maxEntries` | `number` | `500` | Hard cap on active procedures. Default `500`. Overflow triggers FIFO eviction in the consolidator (scenario 7b.F.2). |
| `memory.procedures.deprecationAgeMs` | `number` | `2592000000` | Procedures with `success_count == 0` AND `use_count == 0` older than this are deprecated. Default `2_592_000_000` (30 days). |
| `memory.consolidation.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `memory.consolidation.intervalMs` | `number` | `21600000` |  |
| `memory.consolidation.cooldownMs` | `number` | `86400000` |  |
| `memory.consolidation.minClusterSize` | `number` | `3` |  |
| `memory.consolidation.maxClustersPerTick` | `number` | `5` |  |
| `memory.consolidation.requireSharedTag` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `memory.consolidation.distillTimeoutMs` | `number` | `45000` |  |
| `memory.voting.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master switch. When `false` the vote sub-call is skipped, decay does not run, and the lesson recall reranker treats every row as if `vote_score = 0`. Default `true`. |
| `memory.voting.maxVotePerItem` | `number` | `50` | Clamp on `\|vote_score\|`. Each UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE is `+1`/`-1` and the row is pinned in `[-maxVotePerItem, +maxVotePerItem]`. Must be > 0; bootstrap rejects 0. Default `50`. |
| `memory.voting.signalDecay` | `number` | `0.95` | Per-tick scaling factor applied to every `vote_score` value on the consolidator tick. Range `(0, 1]`; `1.0` disables decay, `0.95` matches the spec default. Bootstrap rejects `<= 0` and `> 1`. Default `0.95`. |
| `memory.voting.scoreBlend` | `number` | `0.6` | Weight of `vote_score` in `combinedScore = scoreBlend * vote_score + (1 - scoreBlend) * (success_count - failure_count)`. Range `[0, 1]`. Default `0.6`. |
| `memory.voting.eventLogMaxRows` | `number` | `50000` | FIFO cap on the `vote_events` audit log. Default `50_000`; `0` disables eviction (the row count is then bounded only by disk space). |
| `memory.voting.profileFilterThreshold` | `number` | `3` | Minimum `\|vote_score\|` at which a `profile_facts` row is hidden from `### profile`. Negative votes ≤ `-profileFilterThreshold` mute the fact; positive scores never hide a fact. Default `3`. |
| `memory.retrieve.rewriter.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `memory.retrieve.rewriter.timeoutMs` | `number` | `10000` |  |
| `memory.retrieve.rewriter.historyTurns` | `number` | `3` |  |
| `memory.retrieve.rewriter.gateMode` | `'always' \| 'heuristic' \| 'embedding'` | `"heuristic"` |  |
| `memory.retrieve.rewriter.embeddingGate.threshold` | `number` | `0.65` |  |
| `memory.retrieve.rewriter.embeddingGate.exemplars` | `string[] \| null` | `null` |  |

## skills

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `skills.catalogTokenBudget` | `number` | `512` | Soft budget for the `### skills` catalog in the stable prefix, in tokens. `buildSkillCatalog` converts it to a char cap at `SKILL_CATALOG_CHARS_PER_TOKEN` (8) chars/token and drops catalog entries past the cap so the prompt stays bounded. Env `ATOMIC_AGENT_SKILLS_CATALOG_BUDGET` wins when set. |
| `skills.disabled` | `string[]` | `[]` | Names of installed skills that should be hidden from the registry. A disabled name is filtered out of `SkillRegistry.list()` entirely — the catalog row in `### skills` disappears and `skill.view` returns `SkillNotFoundError`. Mirrors `UserConfigFile.skills.disabled`. Editing the list invalidates KV-cache once because the stable prefix changes. |
| `skills.cloudWorkspaces` | `CloudWorkspaceSkillsPolicy[]` | `[]` |  |
| `skills.projectTrust` | `ProjectTrustRecord[]` | `[]` | Per-folder trust answers for project skills and instruction files. Mirrors `UserConfigFile.skills.projectTrust`. |
| `skills.taps` | `string[]` | `["anthropics/skills","openai/skills","vercel-labs/agent-skills"]` | GitHub `owner/repo` repositories the skill hub browses for installable SKILL.md skills. Mirrors `UserConfigFile.skills.taps`. |
| `skills.clawhub.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` |  |
| `skills.clawhub.apiBase` | `string` | `"https://clawhub.ai"` |  |
| `skills.clawhub.browseLimit` | `number` | `100` |  |
| `skills.clawhub.nonSuspiciousOnly` | `boolean` | `true` |  |

## tui

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tui.theme` | `string` | `"auto"` |  |
| `tui.whileBusySubmit` | `'steer' \| 'queue'` | `"steer"` |  |
| `tui.mouse` | `boolean` | `true` | Turns terminal mouse reporting on: clicking panels, list rows, the nav bar and the prompt, plus wheel scrolling. Turning it off restores the terminal's own drag-to-select, which mouse reporting takes over — see `/mouse` and `--no-mouse`. Older files are upgraded with `mouse: true`. |
| `tui.showSteps` | `boolean` | `false` | Always show steps (ATO-963): keep every finished turn's tool cards and reasoning open in the chat, as before. Off by default: a finished turn folds into one "Used 6 tools · 40s" line. Additive and unversioned, a file without it reads `false`. A display preference only; the agent never reads it. |
| `tui.notify.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Off means the terminal is never written to out of band. |
| `tui.notify.minDurationMs` | `number` | `30000` | How long a turn must have run before its *successful* ending is worth a ping. A failure always pings regardless: it is the ending that needs a person, and it can happen in two seconds. |
| `tui.sessionRail.order` | `string[]` | `[]` |  |
| `tui.sessionRail.pinned` | `string[]` | `[]` | Session ids pinned to the top of the rail. Pinned rows form a block above everything else; inside the block they follow `order` like any other row. A pinned id that no longer exists is ignored on read and dropped on the next write. |
| `tui.onboarding.completedAt` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `tui.onboarding.importOfferedAt` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `tui.onboarding.introSeenAt` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `tui.onboarding.localSetupSeenAt` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `tui.onboarding.proposedSecondBackendAt` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |
| `tui.onboarding.skippedAt` | `string \| null` | `null` |  |

## analytics

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `analytics.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Anonymous product analytics (PostHog). Older files are transparently upgraded with `analytics: { enabled: true }`. Opt-out only via this flag — set `enabled: false` to disable. Only `{ provider, model }` plus a random anonymous install id are sent; message content, file paths, tool arguments, and the machine's IP are never transmitted (see `src/analytics/`). |

## telegram

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `telegram.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Master kill switch. When `false`, the channel is constructed but never started. |
| `telegram.ownerUserId` | `number \| null` | `null` | Numeric Telegram user id of the sole permitted operator. `null` means "not configured yet" — the channel refuses to start until an id is set (manually or via the slice-3 pairing flow). |
| `telegram.parseMode` | `'plain' \| 'html'` | `"html"` | Render mode for agent-driven outbound replies. Defaults to `"html"` (markdown → Telegram HTML subset). Set `"plain"` to disable formatting entirely — useful as an escape hatch if the formatter ever misbehaves in the wild. |
| `telegram.progressIndicator` | `boolean` | `true` | Live progress indicator in the Telegram channel: a single editable "Thinking…" bubble that mirrors the turn's activity and deletes itself when the reply lands. Enabled by default; `false` is the kill switch if the always-on behavior surprises anyone in production. |

## discord

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `discord.enabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Master kill switch. `false` constructs the channel but never starts it. |
| `discord.ownerUserIds` | `string[]` | `[]` | Discord snowflakes of every permitted operator. **Strings**, not numbers: snowflakes exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, so parsing one as a number silently corrupts the last digits and would let the wrong account drive the agent. Empty means unpaired — the channel refuses every message until at least one id is set. |

## swarm

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `swarm.units` | `SwarmUnitConfig[]` | `[]` | Extra Telegram / Discord bots ("swarm units"). Older files are transparently upgraded with `{ units: [] }`. |

## notifications

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notifications.downloads.channel` | `DownloadNotifyChannelSetting \| null` | `null` | `null` means the operator has not been asked yet: the Models tab asks once, the first time a pull starts, and remembers the answer here. `"off"` is a remembered "no". |

## atomicMail

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `atomicMail.address` | `string \| null` | `null` | `name@atomicmail.ai`, once registered. |
| `atomicMail.accountId` | `string \| null` | `null` | The JMAP account id that goes with it. |
| `atomicMail.ownerEmail` | `string \| null` | `null` | Where the operator wants to be reached. |
| `atomicMail.ownerVerifiedAt` | `string \| null` | `null` | ISO time the operator typed the code back; `null` = not yet. |
| `atomicMail.pendingVerification` | `{ email: string; codeHash: string; expiresAt: string; attempts: number; } \| null` | `null` | A code has been sent and not yet typed back. Never the code itself. |

## git

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git.remoteSync` | `boolean` | `false` | `false` keeps every repository local-only; the safe default. |

## composio

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `composio.enabled` | `boolean` | `true` | Master kill switch. `false` keeps the integration dormant even when a key is present — the escape hatch for an operator who wants the key on disk but the toolkits off. |
| `composio.apiKeyEnv` | `string` | `"COMPOSIO_API_KEY"` | Name of the env var holding the API key. |
| `composio.userId` | `string \| null` | `null` | Stable anonymous install id scoping Composio connected accounts. Minted once as a random UUID and never derived from the operator's email: Composio's docs advise against emails as user ids, and an email is PII the integration has no reason to disclose. Losing it means re-authorising every connected app, so it is persisted. |
| `composio.sessionId` | `string \| null` | `null` | Cached tool-router session id (`trs_…`), so a boot costs no API call. |
| `composio.mcpUrl` | `string \| null` | `null` | Cached MCP endpoint for `sessionId`. |

## mcp

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mcp.servers` | `McpServerConfig[]` | `[]` | MCP client servers. Each entry declares one external MCP server the runtime will connect to at bootstrap and whose tools / resources / prompts will be exposed through the agent's tool registry (namespaced as `mcp.<server>.<tool>`). Older files are transparently upgraded with `mcp: { servers: [] }`. |

## Environment variables

Read from the process environment or from `~/.atomic-agent/.env` (a variable already set in the environment wins over the file). "Overrides" names the config key a variable wins over; the rest exist only as environment variables. `atomic-agent config env` prints this table.

| Variable | Default | Overrides | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_STATE_DIR` | `"~/.atomic-agent"` | env only | State directory: config.json, .env, sessions, memory, models and traces. Shared by the terminal agent and the desktop app. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_GRAMMARS_DIR` | unset | env only | Folder with the tool-call grammars. Unset: the copy shipped next to the binary. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_MAX_TOKENS` | unset | `localModels.completionMaxTokens` | Cap on tokens one local-model reply may produce, 64 to 131072. Wins over the config value when set. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | unset | `localModels.requestTimeoutMs` | Budget of one local-model request (the idle gap for a stream), in ms. Wins over the config value when set. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_SKILLS_CATALOG_BUDGET` | unset | `skills.catalogTokenBudget` | Token budget of the skills list in the prompt, 1 to 100000. Wins over the config value when set. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BROWSER_CDP_URL` | unset | `browser.cdpUrl` | Attach the browser tools to an already running Chrome at this DevTools URL. Wins over the config value when set. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_API_KEY` | unset | env only | API key sent to the local model server. Unset: the managed server's own key, or none. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS` | `3000` | env only | Timeout of one health check of the local model server, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT_MS` | `1800000` | env only | How long a local stream may wait for its first token, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_STREAM_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS` | `21600000` | env only | Backstop on one whole streaming reply from a local model, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_HEALTH_RETRIES` | `5` | env only | Health-check attempts before the local model server counts as down. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_HEALTH_BACKOFF_MS` | `500` | env only | Pause between health-check attempts, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_COMPLETION_RETRIES` | `3` | env only | Retries of a failed local completion request. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_COMPLETION_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS` | `150` | env only | Pause between local completion retries, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LLAMA_DEFAULT_SLOT` | `0` | env only | llama.cpp slot id used for the chat. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_STABLE_PREFIX_SALT` | `"atomic-agent-v1"` | env only | Salt of the prompt-prefix hash. Changing it invalidates cached prompt prefixes. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOADED_TOOLS_CAP` | `8` | env only | How many rarely used tool schemas a session keeps loaded, 1 to 64. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOADED_TOOLS_MAX_TOKENS` | `600` | env only | Token cap of the loaded-tools prompt section, 0 to 8000. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_AUTO_EXPAND_RARE_ON_ERROR` | `true` | env only | Attach a rare tool's full schema after the tool fails. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS` | `8` | env only | Soft cap on tool calls in one step, 1 to 16. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BATCH_TOOL_RESULT_CHAR_CAP` | `32000` | env only | Cap on the combined characters of all tool results in one step. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_SHELL_TOOL_RESULT_CHAR_CAP` | `16000` | env only | Cap on the characters of one shell command result the model sees. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_SHELL_TOOL_RESULT_TAIL_LINES` | `500` | env only | How many last lines of a shell command result the model sees. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOOP_WARNING_THRESHOLD` | `3` | env only | Repeats of the same call before the model is told it is not making progress. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOOP_CRITICAL_THRESHOLD` | `5` | env only | Identical call-and-result streak that blocks the next identical call. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOOP_BREAKER_VETO_STREAK` | `3` | env only | Blocked calls in a row before the agent is made to reply instead. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOOP_HISTORY_SIZE` | `30` | env only | How many recent calls the loop detector remembers. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOOP_WANDERING_THRESHOLD` | `6` | env only | Calls with varied arguments to one tool before the model is redirected. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_LOOP_WANDERING_ESCALATION` | `12` | env only | Calls with varied arguments to one tool before the agent is made to reply. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_REPLY_POLISH` | `true` | env only | Clean up the final reply before a chat surface shows it. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BROWSER_ENABLED` | `true` | env only | Register the browser tools. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BROWSER_CHANNEL` | `"chrome"` | env only | Browser to launch: chrome, msedge or chromium. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BROWSER_HEADLESS` | `false` | env only | Run the agent's browser without a window. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` | unset | env only | Path of the browser binary to launch instead of the channel's default. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BROWSER_NO_SANDBOX` | `false` | env only | Launch the browser without its sandbox (some containers need this). |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_BROWSER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS` | `30000` | env only | How long to wait for the browser to start, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_ENABLED` | `true` | env only | Background task queue. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `3` | env only | Attempts before a failing task is marked failed. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_BACKOFF_INITIAL_MS` | `1000` | env only | First retry delay of a failed task, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_BACKOFF_MAX_MS` | `60000` | env only | Longest retry delay of a failed task, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_RUN_ON_CREATE` | `true` | env only | Start a task as soon as it is created. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_STALE_AFTER_MS` | `300000` | env only | A running task with no progress for this long is put back in the queue, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_SCHEDULER_ENABLED` | `true` | env only | Scheduler that wakes up timed and repeating tasks. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_SCHEDULER_TICK_MS` | `5000` | env only | Scheduler polling interval, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_SCHEDULER_BATCH` | `10` | env only | Most due tasks started per scheduler tick. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_AGENT_TOOLS_ENABLED` | `true` | env only | Let the agent schedule, list and cancel tasks itself. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` | `1000` | env only | Shortest allowed interval of a repeating task, in ms. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_TASKS_REPORT_QUIET_HOURS` | unset | env only | Hold task reports in this local-time window and send one digest after it, e.g. 23:00-08:00. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_STATUS_SNAPSHOT_EVERY_STEPS` | `10` | env only | Post a status snapshot of a long run every this many steps; 0 turns it off. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_STATUS_SNAPSHOT_EVERY_MS` | `300000` | env only | Post a status snapshot of a long run this often, in ms; 0 turns it off. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_UPDATE_CHECK_ON_STARTUP` | `true` | env only | Check GitHub Releases for a newer version when the TUI starts. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_REPO` | `"AtomicBot-ai/atomic-agent"` | env only | GitHub owner/repo used for update checks and self-update. |
| `ATOMIC_AGENT_ANALYTICS` | unset | env only | Set to off to turn anonymous analytics and crash reports off for this process, whatever analytics.enabled says. Not saved. |
| `DO_NOT_TRACK` | unset | env only | Set to 1 to turn analytics and crash reports off, the same as ATOMIC_AGENT_ANALYTICS=off. |

Provider API keys (`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and the rest) are also read from the environment or `.env`; the provider settings in the TUI and the desktop app write them for you.
